clue.text: Heavy material left in Welsh lake by Soviet extremists

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the name of the Welsh lake

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales

indicators.note: the extremes of the word Soviet are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something weighty dumped in a Welsh lake by hardliners from the old USSR.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BALA; 'extremists' takes the first and last letters of 'Soviet', S and T. BALA is a lake in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is weighty stuff carried low in a ship's hold to keep it steady.

clue.text: Shrub found by bishop on leisurely stroll

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ramble is an unhurried walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: A bush spotted by a clergyman on a gentle walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble is a prickly bush, the blackberry plant.

clue.text: On the rocks? Not with this floating asset

definitions.text: On the rocks? Not with this floating asset

parts.words: On the rocks? Not with this floating asset
parts.note: a moored vessel carrying a beacon warns shipping off dangerous shoals, so no one runs aground while it is there

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' tempts one towards drinks served over ice; it means shipwrecked, which this guiding vessel prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored ship with a beacon, marking hazards where a lighthouse cannot stand.

clue.text: Declare invalid, removing article from book

indicators.note: the article is taken out of the synonym for book

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An official rules a document void and strips a clause from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' drops one A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to cancel it officially, as if it never existed.

clue.text: Discharge sailor displaying change of attitude

indicators.note: the sailor is shown off within the phrase for discharge, held inside it

parts.note: to turn out is to expel or discharge
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sacked seaman shows a sudden change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' is an unusual container signal: the phrase for discharge shows the sailor held in its middle. 'Discharge' tempts as a verb meaning fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a complete reversal of opinion or policy.

clue.text: A speed reached by soldiers with a Greek vessel

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A fast pace achieved by troops carrying an ancient Greek pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reached by' and 'with' simply string the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled jar used in ancient Greece to hold wine or oil.

clue.text: Drink swallowed very quietly — a temptation once!

indicators.note: the drink takes the musical letters inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A drink downed in secret, a lure from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' signals the drink taking in the musical direction. The exclamation points to Eve's temptation in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The forbidden fruit Eve took in Eden is traditionally pictured as an apple.

clue.text: This represents a word for a North Briton with no pulse

parts.note: the Picts were ancient people of northern Scotland
O is nought or zero, meaning none
gram is a kind of pulse, a chickpea or similar bean

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry describing a Scotsman who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links definition and wordplay; 'with no pulse' paints a corpse but supplies O and GRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictogram is a picture symbol standing for a whole word or idea.

clue.text: Bracing air an individual associated with a wizard place

indicators.note: the individual is linked on after the wizard's land, so it follows it

parts.note: Oz is the magical land of the Wizard of Oz
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Fresh air and a lone figure linked with a magical land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' tacks the individual on after the land of the Wizard of Oz, so the clue's second piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly used for fresh, invigorating seaside air.

clue.text: How like a winter Shakespeare's had been

definitions.text: How like a winter Shakespeare's had been

parts.words: How like a winter Shakespeare's had been
parts.note: the clue quotes Sonnet 97, 'How like a winter hath my ... been', asking for the word missing from the line

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's sonnet compares time apart from the beloved to a bleak winter; the missing word is that time apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The sonnet's speaker is away from the beloved, and that time apart is the word the line needs.

clue.text: Gaseous element a man' discovered around Gateshead

indicators.note: the man's name goes around the single letter

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, a typical crossword source of letters
the head of the word Gate, its first letter, read from Gate's head

explanation.surface: A chemical element was found by some chap near the town of Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gateshead', a town on Tyneside in north-east England, is read as 'Gate's head', the first letter G; 'around' puts RON round it after A. The stray apostrophe after 'man' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, one of the chemical elements found in air.

clue.text: Grasping parent in car, returning with evidence of debts

indicators.note: the parent goes inside the turned-round car
the word car is written backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself
Pa is a familiar word for father, a parent
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A greedy father in the family car, back home with a pile of unpaid bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns only the car round, giving RAC; 'in' then sets the parent inside that, and the debt notes follow. 'Grasping' looks like holding on, but means greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means greedy for gain, grabbing all one can.

clue.text: Weapon for a domineering' woman

definitions.meaning: a broad-headed axe used in medieval fighting
a bossy, aggressive older woman, an informal insult

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just links the two senses; the apostrophe after 'domineering' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval war axe gave its name to a forceful, overbearing woman, both senses sharing the one word.

clue.text: Main element in viva voce, an inquisition

indicators.note: an element is a part, so the answer is a part found inside these words

explanation.surface: The chief part of an oral exam is a grilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'voce, an'. A viva voce is an oral examination, so the surface sounds like talk of exams. 'Main' is old poetic usage for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary name for the high sea, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Woman removes head of chapel

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym for chapel is dropped

parts.note: a bethel is a nonconformist chapel or seamen's place of worship

explanation.surface: A woman ousts the leader of her congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removes head of' drops the B from BETHEL. Bethel is a name used for a Methodist or Baptist chapel in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Tragic Latin hero — one of exceptional courage

indicators.note: a tragic event wrecks things, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A doomed Roman hero, a man of remarkable bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic' rearranges LATIN HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionheart is a name for a very brave person, as in King Richard I.

clue.text: Books of a woman sage written in a different way

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible
her is a pronoun standing for a woman
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: Volumes by a wise woman were composed in an unusual style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently, in some other manner.

clue.text: Such a labour, making her char around University

indicators.note: the cleaning word goes round the letter for University

parts.note: to char is to do cleaning work, so char means clean

explanation.surface: A charwoman's mighty task of cleaning around a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts CLEAN round U to give CULEAN. A char, or charwoman, is a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Herculean task is one demanding vast strength, like the twelve labours of Hercules.

clue.text: When one's caught inside, better to ad-lib

indicators.note: the contracted pronoun phrase is trapped within the word for better

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
one is I, so one's means I is

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a batsman out caught should do better at making it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught inside' signals the container; 'one's' is I'S, the Roman one with its 's. The cricket sense of caught is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to make it up on the spot without preparation.

clue.text: Champion is terrific when drinking wine!

indicators.note: the word for terrific takes in the wine, as if swallowing it

parts.note: terrific and super both mean excellent
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A fan says winning is wonderful once the wine is flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drinking' signals the word for terrific taking in the wine. 'Champion' looks like a noun for a winner but means a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back it, so a champion is a backer.

clue.text: Wind thus restricting heads of relief organization, on business

indicators.note: the Latin word holds the initials inside it, hemming them in

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as given

indicators.note: the first letters of the two following words

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A gale threatens aid workers' chiefs while they are on official duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of' gives R and O; 'restricting' signals the Latin word hemming them in; 'on' places the business abbreviation after.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Half-heartedly cleaned up the bike

indicators.note: the heart of the word is a doubled letter, and only half of it is kept

parts.note: mopped means wiped up with a mop

explanation.surface: Someone tidied up the bicycle without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of MOPPED is PP; 'Half-heartedly' keeps only one P. A moped is a low-powered motorbike with pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorised two-wheeler with pedals.

clue.text: Decrepit stranger in the borders of Dahomey

indicators.note: the word for stranger sits within those edge letters
the edges of the word Dahomey are its first and last letters

parts.note: odder and stranger both mean more peculiar

explanation.surface: A frail foreigner on the frontier of the old African state of Dahomey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the borders of' gives D and Y; 'in' puts ODDER between them. Dahomey is the old name of Benin.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery means shaky and feeble through age.

clue.text: Huge bird eating a hard fish

indicators.note: the bird takes the A inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An enormous bird devours a tough fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts A inside ROC to give ROAC, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Accept a foreign currency — it is underwritten

indicators.note: in a down entry, being written underneath means coming after

parts.note: DM is the Deutschmark, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Take on some foreign money: an insurer guarantees it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is underwritten' means IT is written under A and DM, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to accept or concede it.

clue.text: It can serve as tinder, barring ill luck!

definitions.meaning: rotten, crumbly wood that catches a spark easily
a saying used to ward off misfortune after a hopeful remark

explanation.walkthrough: Touchwood is rotten wood that lights easily; saying 'touch wood' is the British form of 'knock on wood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed wood used to start fires shares its name with the phrase said, while tapping wood, to avert bad luck.

clue.text: Theist's first observance, worn out by constant repetition

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Theist's is used

parts.note: a rite is a religious observance or ceremony

explanation.surface: A believer's chief religious ceremony, faded by being done over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'Theist's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means stale and hackneyed from overuse.

clue.text: Holy books found in bird sanctuary

indicators.note: the bible abbreviation is located inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
AV, the Authorized Version, is the King James Bible

explanation.surface: Bibles discovered in a bird reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals the container. 'bird sanctuary' reads as one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a place of safety or refuge.

clue.text: Temporary quarters by river, sited around a bell-tower

indicators.note: the two pieces are set on either side of the letter A

parts.note: a camp is a temporary place to live, as tents or huts
the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: Soldiers camp beside a river, their tents pitched round a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sited around' signals the two pieces flanking the A; 'by' just places them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a freestanding bell tower, typical of Italian churches.

clue.text: Possibly active part for musicians?

definitions.meaning: in grammar, active is one form a verb takes, alongside passive
a line in a piece of music, such as the alto line in a choir

explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks active as one example of the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls active and passive two forms of the verb, and a choral score is split into parts for each singer.

clue.text: A group broke bread, some say, after a month

indicators.note: the sounded part comes after the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: a homophone signal: the past tense of eat, as many British speakers say it, rhymes with bet

parts.note: to break bread is to eat, so broke bread means ate

explanation.surface: A party shared a meal, apparently, once a month had passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' points to the British pronunciation of 'ate' to rhyme with 'bet', which ETTE echoes. OCTETTE is an older spelling of octet.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a set of eight, usually musicians performing together.

clue.text: Head off jogger in New York from the convent

indicators.note: the shortened runner goes inside the abbreviation for New York
the first letter of the synonym for jogger is cut away

parts.note: a jogger is one who runs, a runner

explanation.surface: A command to intercept a jogger in Manhattan as she leaves the convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' leaves UNNER; 'in' signals that going inside the abbreviation. 'Head off' reads as intercept in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a religious house where nuns live.
